raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan.

---

I'm 68 now, been farming this land for 35 years. My wife and I, plus our son's family — seven mouths, though two of the young ones are in school and my son works in town most of the year. So for the field work, it's really me and my wife, and the daughter-in-law helps in the busy season.

I have 16.1 mu. Most of it is cotton — that's what grows here in our village, that's what the buyers come for. I've tried other things over the years but cotton is what I know. I keep about 4 mu for stevia because the company signed a contract with several of us in the village two years ago and the price was decent. My neighbor Lao Wang does the same.

**Cotton, about 12 mu.** I'll plant end of April like always, after the soil warms up. The Bt cotton seed from the agricultural supply shop — everyone uses it now, the bollworm damage used to be terrible before. About 30 yuan per mu for seed. I plow with the small tractor I rent from my cousin, takes two days.

For fertilizer, I put a compound fertilizer before planting — one bag per mu, the 15-15-15 kind, that's about 50 jin. Then when the cotton is flowering I topdress some urea, maybe half a bag per mu. Last year I tried skipping the topdress because money was tight and the yield dropped a bit — my neighbor warned me not to do that again. So this year I'll do it properly. That works out to maybe 13 kg of nitrogen per mu total, which is what most of us around here do.

Irrigation — I have the well, but the electricity for pumping isn't cheap. Cotton doesn't need as much water as wheat. I'll water once before planting to wet the ground, once at flowering if it's dry. Two times usually enough if the summer rains come.

Pesticide is the expensive part. Herbicide before emergence, then insecticide two or three times through the summer when I see aphids or bollworm. I walk the field every few days to check. My son bought me a small knapsack sprayer a few years back.

Harvest is the hard part at my age. Three pickings, September through October. The daughter-in-law helps, sometimes we hire two women from the village for a few days. Last year I got about 250 jin of lint per mu — not the best year, not the worst. I'm hoping for the same this year.

**Stevia, about 4.1 mu.** This is more work but the contract price is steady. I buy seedlings from the company, they come in May. Transplant by hand — slow work, the whole family pitches in over a weekend. The company tells us how much fertilizer to use but I mostly follow what the other contract farmers do. A bit less nitrogen than cotton, more potassium they say helps the leaves.

I irrigate stevia more than cotton, maybe three times — the leaves need to stay lush. Harvest is in the fall, cut the plants and dry the leaves. Labor-intensive but the company takes everything.

Total cost, I'm figuring maybe 6,500 yuan for the year across both crops. That's near the limit of what I can put up front. If the cotton price is bad at harvest, it'll be a tight winter.
